title.zh: 卷355 列傳一百四十二 魁伦 广兴 初彭龄
title.en: Volume 355 Biographies 142: Kui Lun, Guang Xing, Chu Peng Ling
title.raw: 卷355 列傳一百四十二 魁伦 广兴 初彭龄

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十二

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 142
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 142

sentences.zh: 魁倫廣興初彭齡

translations.literal: Kui Lun, Guang Xing, and Chu Pengling
translations.idiomatic: Kui Lun, Guang Xing, and Chu Pengling

sentences.zh: 魁倫，完顏氏，滿洲正黃旗人，副將軍查弼納孫也。

translations.literal: Kui Lun, of the Wanyan clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and grandson of the deputy general Zhabina.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Lun, of the Wanyan clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner and a grandson of the deputy general Zhabina.

sentences.zh: 襲世管佐領，兼輕車都尉，授四川漳臘營參將，累擢建昌鎮總兵。

translations.literal: He inherited the hereditary assistant commandant post, also held the title of Commandant of Light Chariots, was appointed a deputy commander in the Zhangla Camp in Sichuan, and was repeatedly promoted to commander-in-chief of Jianchang Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the hereditary assistant commandant post, held the concurrent title of Commandant of Light Chariots, served as deputy commander of the Zhangla Camp in Sichuan, and rose by stages to commander-in-chief of Jianchang Garrison.

sentences.zh: 嘗入覲，高宗詢家世，魁倫陳戰功甚悉。

translations.literal: Once when he came to court for an audience, the Gaozong Emperor inquired into his family background, and Kui Lun set forth his forebears’ military achievements in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: On one audience at court, the Gaozong Emperor asked about his lineage, and Kui Lun recounted his family’s battle honors at length.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十三年，擢福州將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year of Qianlong he was promoted to Fuzhou Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year of the Qianlong reign he was appointed military governor of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 喜聲伎，制行不謹，總督伍拉納欲劾之。

translations.literal: He delighted in music and entertainers and was lax in conduct; Governor-General Wula Na wished to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of music and performers and careless in his conduct, and Governor-General Wula Na sought to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納故貪，逼勒屬吏財賄，复縱洋盜，盜艇集五虎門外不問。

translations.literal: Wula Na was by nature greedy, extorted bribes from subordinate officials, and again indulged foreign pirates, whose boats gathered outside the Wuhu Gate without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Wula Na was notoriously corrupt, squeezed his subordinates for bribes, and winked at foreign pirates, whose vessels clustered outside the Wuhu Gate unchecked.

sentences.zh: 魁倫遂疊疏劾閩省吏治廢弛，伍拉納及巡撫浦霖溺職，按察使錢受椿等迎合助虐。

translations.literal: Kui Lun then sent repeated memorials impeaching the slack administration of Fujian, charging Wula Na and Governor Pu Lin with dereliction, and the surveillance commissioner Qian Shouchun and others with currying favor and abetting oppression.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Lun then filed repeated memorials denouncing Fujian’s collapsed governance, accusing Wula Na and Governor Pu Lin of neglecting duty and Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun and others of flattering their superiors and aiding abuse.

sentences.zh: 上怒，褫伍拉納等職逮問，命長麟署總督，偕魁倫鞫訊，得伍拉納等貪婪及庫藏虧絀狀，俱伏法。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, stripped Wula Na and the others of office and had them arrested for trial, ordered Chang Lin to act as governor-general, and together with Kui Lun conducted the inquiry; the greed of Wula Na and the others and the deficits in the treasury were established, and all were executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, stripped Wula Na and his associates of rank and ordered them arrested; he appointed Chang Lin acting governor-general and had him investigate jointly with Kui Lun. Their corruption and the treasury shortfalls were proved, and all were put to death.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納為和珅姻戚，當按治時，上切責長麟瞻徇，罷去，以事由魁倫舉發，特寬之，代署總督，嚴捕海盜，屢獲其魁。

translations.literal: Wula Na was a relative by marriage of Heshen; when the case was being handled the emperor sharply rebuked Chang Lin for favoritism and removed him. Because the affair had been exposed by Kui Lun, he was specially lenient, made acting governor-general in Chang Lin’s place, strictly hunted pirates, and repeatedly captured their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Wula Na was related by marriage to Heshen. During the prosecution the emperor sharply rebuked Chang Lin for partiality and dismissed him. Because Kui Lun had brought the matter to light, he was treated with special leniency, made acting governor-general, waged a vigorous campaign against pirates, and repeatedly took their ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，實授總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was formally appointed governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign he received a regular appointment as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 三年，巨盜林發枝投首，海患稍戢。

translations.literal: In the third year the great pirate Lin Fazhi surrendered, and the maritime threat was somewhat quelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the notorious pirate Lin Fazhi gave himself up, and the coastal menace eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 以母憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 自治閩獄。

translations.literal: He had himself governed the Fujian cases.
translations.idiomatic: He had personally directed the Fujian prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 以伉直聞於時，仁宗尤眷之。

translations.literal: He was known in his time for blunt uprightness, and the Renzong Emperor especially favored him.
translations.idiomatic: He was known throughout the age for blunt integrity, and the Renzong Emperor held him in special regard.

sentences.zh: 四年，起署吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was recalled to serve as acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was recalled from mourning to serve as acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 魁倫屢於上前自稱昔治四川啯匪功，謂賊不難辦，請赴軍前，時上督責諸將平賊甚急，經略勒保未稱帝意，命魁倫赴四川，逮勒保治罪，即代署總督，駐達州治軍餉。

translations.literal: Kui Lun repeatedly told the emperor before him of his past achievements in suppressing the Gelo bandits in Sichuan, saying the rebels were not hard to deal with, and asked to go to the front. At that time the emperor was urgently pressing the generals to pacify the rebels; the commander-in-chief Lebao had not satisfied the emperor’s wishes. Kui Lun was ordered to Sichuan, Lebao was arrested and punished, and Kui Lun at once acted as governor-general, stationed at Dazhou to manage military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Before the throne Kui Lun often boasted of his earlier success against the Gelo bandits in Sichuan, claiming the rebels would be easy to crush, and begged to take the field. The emperor was then urgently pressing his generals to end the rebellion; Commander-in-Chief Lebao had failed to please him. Kui Lun was sent to Sichuan, Lebao was arrested for punishment, and Kui Lun immediately became acting governor-general, basing himself at Dazhou to oversee army provisions.

sentences.zh: 勒保獲譴由蜚語，既就逮，所部訴其冤，乞代奏，魁倫稍稍為置辯，終以玩誤軍務讞擬重闢，軍心因之渙散，不為用。

translations.literal: Lebao’s punishment arose from rumor; once he was arrested his subordinates pleaded his innocence and begged someone to memorialize on his behalf. Kui Lun made some effort to speak for him, but in the end the finding was dereliction of military duty with a recommendation of heavy execution. Army morale therefore dissolved and he was of no use.
translations.idiomatic: Lebao’s disgrace sprang from slander; after his arrest his troops protested his innocence and asked that their plea be forwarded. Kui Lun offered a measure of defense, yet the final verdict still charged him with bungling the campaign and recommended the heaviest penalty. Morale collapsed and the army would not follow Kui Lun.

sentences.zh: 額勒登保繼為經略，與德楞泰先後赴甘肅剿竄匪，魁倫專任四川軍事。

translations.literal: Eledengbao succeeded as commander-in-chief; he and Delin Tai went in turn to Gansu to suppress the roving bandits, while Kui Lun bore sole responsibility for Sichuan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Eledengbao became commander-in-chief; he and Delin Tai went in succession to Gansu to hunt down roving bandits, while Kui Lun alone handled military affairs in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 五年春，冉天元糾數路殘匪潛匿大竹，魁倫逡巡未發，賊脅眾數万由定遠渡嘉陵江，圖擾川西，魁倫繞道鄰水，自順慶追剿，檄總兵七十五還守重慶。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Ran Tianyuan gathered remnant bandits from several routes and lay hidden in Dazhu. Kui Lun hesitated and did not move. The rebels mustered tens of thousands, crossed the Jialing River at Dingyuan, and intended to ravage western Sichuan. Kui Lun took a detour through Linshui and pursued from Shunqing, ordering Commander-in-Chief No. 75 to return and guard Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year Ran Tianyuan rallied remnant bands from several routes and hid in Dazhu. Kui Lun dallied and did not strike. The rebels raised a host of tens of thousands, crossed the Jialing at Dingyuan, and aimed to ravage western Sichuan. Kui Lun detoured through Linshui and gave chase from Shunqing, while ordering Commander-in-Chief No. 75 back to hold Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 上以數年來賊氛皆在川東北，惟川西完善，地為軍餉所出，斥魁倫疏防，革職留任。

translations.literal: For years the rebel threat had lain in northeastern Sichuan, while western Sichuan alone remained intact and was the source of army provisions. The emperor rebuked Kui Lun for lax defense, stripped his office but retained him in post.
translations.idiomatic: For years the rebels had troubled only northeastern Sichuan, while the west stayed intact and supplied the army’s grain. The emperor denounced Kui Lun’s negligent defense, removed his rank but kept him on duty.

sentences.zh: 賊尋渡江掠蓬溪，諸將獨總兵硃射鬥力戰而兵少，魁倫約為接應復不至，射鬥戰死。

translations.literal: The rebels soon crossed the river and plundered Pengxi. Among the generals only Commander-in-Chief Zhu Shedou fought hard with too few men. Kui Lun had promised reinforcements but again did not come; Shedou died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon crossed again and looted Pengxi. Of all the generals only Zhu Shedou fought fiercely with too few troops. Kui Lun had promised support but once more failed to arrive, and Shedou fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 魁倫退屯潼川​​，降三品頂戴，詔責嚴守潼河，曰：「此爾生死關頭也！」

translations.literal: Kui Lun withdrew and encamped at Tongchuan, was reduced to third-rank insignia, and was ordered by edict to hold the Tong River strictly, with the words: “This is the hinge of your life and death!”
translations.idiomatic: Kui Lun fell back to Tongchuan, was demoted to third-rank insignia, and received an edict to guard the Tong River at all costs: “Your life and death hang on this!”

sentences.zh: 復起勒保為四川提督，偕德楞泰進剿川西、川北。

translations.literal: Lebao was again raised up as Sichuan provincial military commissioner and advanced with Delin Tai to suppress western and northern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lebao was restored as Sichuan provincial military commissioner and marched with Delin Tai to suppress the west and north of the province.

sentences.zh: 四月，賊伺川西備嚴，乘間竄渡潼河，焚太和，逼成都，上怒魁倫屢失機縱賊，褫職逮問，命勒保代署總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the rebels, seeing western Sichuan heavily guarded, slipped across the Tong River, burned Taihe, and pressed on Chengdu. The emperor was enraged that Kui Lun had repeatedly missed chances and let the rebels go, stripped him of office and arrested him for trial, and ordered Lebao to act as governor-general in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the rebels, finding western Sichuan well defended, stole across the Tong River, burned Taihe, and threatened Chengdu. The emperor raged that Kui Lun had again lost his chance and let them escape, stripped him and ordered his arrest, and appointed Lebao acting governor-general.

sentences.zh: 侍郎周興岱往會鞫，尋逮克賜死，子扎拉芬戍伊犁。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Zhou Xingdai went to join the inquiry; soon Kui Lun was arrested and granted death, and his son Zhala Fen was banished to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Zhou Xingdai went to assist the investigation; Kui Lun was soon arrested and granted suicide, and his son Zhala Fen was exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 魁倫居官廉，自為尚書時，詔寬減閩關賠繳銀六千兩，至是罄家產不足償，上益憐之，給還宅一區，俾其妻有所棲止；

translations.literal: Kui Lun had been upright in office. While he was still Minister of Personnel an edict had remitted six thousand taels of his indemnity for the Fujian customs. Now he exhausted his family property and still could not pay; the emperor pitied him all the more, returned one residence, and allowed his wife a place to live.
translations.idiomatic: Kui Lun had served with integrity. As Minister of Personnel he had already been granted remission of six thousand taels owed from the Fujian customs levy. Now he spent his entire estate and still fell short; the emperor pitied him further, restored one house, and gave his wife a roof over her head.

sentences.zh: 又因其孫幼稚，命扎拉芬到戍三年釋歸，宣諭廷臣，使知法戒焉。

translations.literal: Because his grandson was young, Zhala Fen was ordered to serve three years at the frontier and then released. The emperor announced this to the court so all might know the lesson of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Because his grandson was still a child, Zhala Fen was ordered to complete three years on the frontier before returning. The emperor proclaimed this to the court as a warning drawn from the law.

sentences.zh: 廣興，字賡虞，滿洲鑲黃旗人，大學士高晉第十二子。

translations.literal: Guang Xing, style name Gengyu, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and the twelfth son of Grand Secretary Gao Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Xing, courtesy name Gengyu, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner and the twelfth son of Grand Secretary Gao Jin.

sentences.zh: 入貲為主事，補官禮部。

translations.literal: He entered office by purchase as a director and was appointed in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way in as a director and received appointment in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敏於任事，背誦案牘如瀉水，大學士王杰器其才。

translations.literal: Quick in handling affairs, he recited documents from memory like pouring water; Grand Secretary Wang Jie valued his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was brisk in business and could recite case papers from memory as fluently as running water; Grand Secretary Wang Jie admired his ability.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，首劾和珅罪狀，擢副都御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was the first to impeach Heshen’s crimes and was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he led the impeachment of Heshen’s crimes and was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 命赴四川治軍需，綜覈精嚴，月節糜費數十萬金，為時所忌，以騷擾驛傳被劾，上優容之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to Sichuan to manage military supplies, audited with exacting care, and each month saved hundreds of thousands in waste. He was envied by his contemporaries and impeached for harassing courier stations, but the emperor treated him leniently.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Sichuan to manage army supplies, audited with ruthless precision, and saved hundreds of thousands of taels each month in waste. Envy bred impeachments for harassing the courier network, but the emperor showed him forbearance.

sentences.zh: 复屢與總督魁倫互劾，召還，左遷通政副使。

translations.literal: Again he repeatedly impeached Governor-General Kui Lun in turn; he was recalled and demoted to vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He and Governor-General Kui Lun traded impeachments again and again; recalled to the capital, he was demoted to vice commissioner of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 九年，擢兵部侍郎，兼副都統、總管內務府大臣，署刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was promoted to vice minister of war, concurrently vice commander-in-chief and superintendent of the Imperial Household Department, and acting vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became vice minister of war, concurrently vice commander-in-chief and superintendent of the Imperial Household, and acting vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 同僚輕其於刑名非素習，廣興引證律例，屢正誤讞，眾乃服。

translations.literal: Colleagues looked down on him as not practiced in penal matters; Guang Xing cited statutes and repeatedly corrected mistaken verdicts, and the others then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues scoffed that he was no expert in criminal law; Guang Xing cited the code, corrected erroneous verdicts again and again, and won their respect.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奏劾御前大臣定親王綿恩揀選官缺專擅違例，廷臣察詢，不直所言，降三品京堂，罷兼職。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized impeaching the imperial front attendant Prince Ding Mian En for selecting official vacancies in violation of regulations on his own authority. The court investigated and did not uphold his charges; he was demoted to third-rank capital official and stripped of concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he impeached Imperial Front Attendant Prince Ding, Mian En, for usurping authority in filling official vacancies against regulation. The court investigated and found his accusation unsupported; he was demoted to third-rank capital official and lost his concurrent posts.

sentences.zh: 尋補奉宸苑卿，擢刑部侍郎，复兼內務府大臣。

translations.literal: Soon he was made superintendent of the Imperial Parks, promoted to vice minister of justice, and again given the Imperial Household concurrent post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed superintendent of the Imperial Parks, promoted to vice minister of justice, and again given charge of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 上方倚任，廣興亦慷慨直言，召對每逾晷刻。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on him; Guang Xing also spoke boldly and frankly, and each audience ran past the hour.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was leaning heavily on him; Guang Xing spoke with blunt candor, and their audiences often ran past the hour mark.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「汝與初彭齡皆朕信任之人，何外廷怨恨乃爾？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: “You and Chu Pengling are both men I trust—why is the outer court so full of resentment toward you?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “You and Chu Pengling are both men I trust—why does the outer court resent you so bitterly?”

sentences.zh: 廣興頫首謝。

translations.literal: Guang Xing bowed his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Xing bowed his head in acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 數奉使赴山東、河南按事，益作威福，中外側目。

translations.literal: Sent repeatedly on missions to Shandong and Henan to investigate affairs, he increasingly threw his weight about; court and country watched with sidelong glances.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated missions to Shandong and Henan to investigate cases he grew ever more overbearing; the whole court watched him with unease.

sentences.zh: 內監鄂羅哩者，自乾隆中充近侍，年七十馀，嘗至朝廊與廣興坐語，以長者自居。

translations.literal: The eunuch Eluoli had served close to the throne since the Qianlong reign, was over seventy, and once came to the corridor of the court to sit and talk with Guang Xing, putting on the airs of an elder.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Eluoli had attended the throne since the Qianlong years, was over seventy, and once came to the court corridor to sit and chat with Guang Xing, comporting himself as an elder.

sentences.zh: 廣興艴然曰：「汝輩閹人，當敬謹侍立，安得與大臣論世誼乎？」

translations.literal: Guang Xing flushed angrily and said: “You castrated fellows ought to stand respectfully in attendance—how dare you discuss family connections with a great minister?”
translations.idiomatic: Guang Xing flushed and snapped, “You castrated creatures should stand respectfully in attendance—how dare you bandy family ties with a great minister?”

sentences.zh: 鄂羅哩恨次骨，思以中之。

translations.literal: Eluoli hated him to the marrow and sought a way to bring him down.
translations.idiomatic: Eluoli hated him to the bone and plotted to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，內庫給宮中段不如數，且窳敗，鄂羅哩言由廣興剋減，上即命傳諭，出而漫言之，廣興不知為上旨，坐而與辯。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year the inner treasury issued palace silks short in quantity and shoddy in quality. Eluoli said Guang Xing had skimped. The emperor at once ordered a message delivered; Eluoli spoke of it casually outside. Guang Xing did not know it was the emperor’s order and sat debating with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year the inner treasury delivered palace silks short in count and poor in quality. Eluoli blamed Guang Xing for skimping. The emperor ordered a message delivered at once; Eluoli repeated it casually outside. Guang Xing did not know it was imperial instruction and sat arguing with him.

sentences.zh: 鄂羅哩入奏其坐聽諭旨，上怒，一日，面詰廣興，廣興言總管太監孫進忠與庫官勾通，欲交外省織造，藉遂需索規費之計。

translations.literal: Eluoli entered and reported that Guang Xing had sat while listening to the edict. The emperor was enraged. One day he questioned Guang Xing to his face; Guang Xing said Superintendent Eunuch Sun Jinzhong had colluded with treasury officials, wished to hand work to outside weavers, and thereby carried out a scheme to extort customary fees.
translations.idiomatic: Eluoli entered and reported that Guang Xing had remained seated while the edict was read. The emperor raged. One day he confronted Guang Xing directly; Guang Xing said Superintendent Eunuch Sun Jinzhong had colluded with treasury clerks, meant to shift weaving to outside contractors, and thus engineered extortion of customary fees.

sentences.zh: 上以其不能指實庫官何人，挾詐面欺，下廷臣議罪，尋寬之。

translations.literal: Because he could not name which treasury official in fact, and was judged to have deceived the emperor’s face with false charges, the case was sent to the court for punishment; soon he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Because he could not name the treasury official involved and was judged to have lied to the emperor’s face, the matter went to the court for sentencing; he was soon spared.

sentences.zh: 罷職家居，於是與廣興不協者，蜂起媒孽其短。

translations.literal: Dismissed from office and living at home, those at odds with Guang Xing now swarmed to fabricate faults against him.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of office and living at home, those who bore him ill will now swarmed to invent charges against him.

sentences.zh: 上密諭山東、河南兩省巡撫察奏，遂交章劾其奉使時任意作威，苛求供頓，收納餽遺諸罪狀，下獄議絞。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly ordered the governors of Shandong and Henan to investigate and report; memorials then piled up impeaching his arrogance on mission, demanding excessive supplies, accepting gifts, and other crimes, and he was imprisoned with death by strangulation recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered the governors of Shandong and Henan to investigate and report; memorials then flooded in accusing him of bullying on his missions, demanding excessive lodging, accepting bribes, and other crimes, and he was jailed with strangulation recommended.

sentences.zh: 上親廷訊，尚欲緩其獄，廣興未省上意，抗辯無引罪語，而贓私有實據，上益怒，遂置之法，籍其家，子蘊秀戍吉林，並罪兩省官吏及山東言官各有差。

translations.literal: The emperor personally tried him at court and still wished to ease his case. Guang Xing did not grasp the emperor’s intent and argued without words of confession; yet the evidence of embezzlement was solid. The emperor grew still angrier, had him executed, confiscated his property, banished his son Yunxiu to Jilin, and punished officials of both provinces and Shandong censors to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor tried him in open court and still meant to soften the sentence. Guang Xing failed to read his mood and argued without a word of repentance; yet the proof of graft was solid. The emperor’s wrath deepened; Guang Xing was executed, his estate confiscated, his son Yunxiu exiled to Jilin, and officials of both provinces and Shandong censors punished in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 廣興伉爽無城府，疾惡嚴，喜詆人陰私。

translations.literal: Guang Xing was forthright and without hidden designs, severe in hating evil, and fond of exposing others’ private faults.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Xing was blunt and without hidden designs, harsh toward wickedness, and fond of airing others’ private failings.

sentences.zh: 既得志，驕奢日甚，縱情聲色，不能約束奴僕，終及於禍。

translations.literal: Once he had his way, pride and luxury grew daily; he indulged in music and women, could not restrain his servants, and in the end met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had his way, pride and luxury mounted daily; he gave himself to music and women, could not control his servants, and at last brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 初彭齡，字頤園，山東萊陽人。

translations.literal: Chu Pengling, style name Yiyuan, was a native of Laiyang in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pengling, courtesy name Yiyuan, was a native of Laiyang in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十六年，巡幸山東，召試，賜舉人。

translations.literal: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, when the emperor toured Shandong, he was summoned for examination and granted the rank of provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-sixth year of Qianlong, during the imperial tour of Shandong, he was summoned for examination and made a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he passed the metropolitan examination, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed editor.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，遷江南道御史。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year he was transferred to censor of the Jiangnan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year he was transferred to censor of the Jiangnan circuit.

sentences.zh: 劾協辦大學士彭元瑞徇私為婿侄營事，元瑞被黜；

translations.literal: He impeached Associate Grand Secretary Peng Yuanrui for showing favoritism in advancing his son-in-law’s nephew; Yuanrui was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Associate Grand Secretary Peng Yuanrui for favoritism in advancing his son-in-law’s nephew; Yuanrui was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又江西巡撫陳淮以貪著，劾罷之，風采振一時。

translations.literal: Again Jiangxi Governor Chen Huai was notorious for greed; he impeached and removed him, and his reputation shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Governor Chen Huai was likewise notorious for greed; Chu impeached and removed him, and his reputation soared for a time.

sentences.zh: 累遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，出為雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he went out as governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he was appointed governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時總督富綱請罷官鹽，改歸民運民銷，詔下彭齡議。

translations.literal: At that time Governor-General Fu Gang requested abolition of government salt and a shift to private transport and private sale; an edict was sent down for Pengling to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Fu Gang then asked to abolish government salt and shift to private transport and sale; an edict ordered Pengling to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 疏上，略曰：「滇鹽向例官督灶煎，分井定額，按月完納省倉。

translations.literal: In his memorial he stated in summary: “Yunnan salt has customarily been government-supervised at the furnaces, with quotas fixed per well and monthly delivery to the provincial granary.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial summarized: “Yunnan salt has customarily been boiled under government supervision, with quotas set per well and monthly delivery to the provincial granary.

sentences.zh: 行銷之法，按州縣戶口多寡定額，地方官備價運銷交課。

translations.literal: The method of distribution set quotas by the population of each prefecture and county; local officials advanced funds to transport and sell and remit the tax.
translations.idiomatic: Distribution quotas followed each prefecture and county’s household count; local officials advanced funds to transport, sell, and remit the levy.

sentences.zh: 其始灶戶所領官給薪本敷裕，交足額鹽之外，尚有馀鹽；

translations.literal: At first the fuel stipend the furnace households received from the government was ample; beyond filling the quota salt there was surplus salt.
translations.idiomatic: At first the government fuel allowance for furnace households was ample; beyond meeting the quota they still had surplus salt.

sentences.zh: 官售額鹽，扣還腳價之外，尚有馀課。

translations.literal: When the government sold quota salt, beyond deducting transport costs there was surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the government sold the quota salt, transport costs deducted, surplus revenue remained.

sentences.zh: 行之日久，不肖州縣勾通井官，私買額外馀鹽，行銷肥己。

translations.literal: As time went on, unworthy prefects and counties colluded with well officials, privately bought extra surplus salt, and sold it to enrich themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Over time corrupt prefects and counties colluded with well officials, privately bought surplus salt beyond the quota, and sold it for private gain.

sentences.zh: 灶戶利於賣私，益滋偷漏。

translations.literal: Furnace households profited from selling privately and smuggling increased all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Furnace households profited from illicit sales, and smuggling only grew.

sentences.zh: 前巡撫劉秉恬遂令州縣額銷十萬斤者加銷一二萬，以資辦公。

translations.literal: The former governor Liu Bingtian then ordered prefectures and counties with a quota of one hundred thousand jin to sell an extra ten or twenty thousand to fund office expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Former Governor Liu Bingtian then ordered counties with a hundred-thousand-jin quota to sell an extra ten or twenty thousand jin to fund office expenses.

sentences.zh: 灶戶薪本不敷，無力加煎，扌毚和灰土，州縣滯銷，因有派累之事。

translations.literal: Furnace households’ fuel stipends were insufficient and they could not boil more; they adulterated with ash and earth. Prefectures and counties could not sell and therefore imposed forced levies.
translations.idiomatic: Fuel stipends fell short and furnace households could not boil more; they adulterated with ash and earth. Counties could not move the salt and resorted to forced levies.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十六年，鹽道蔣繼勳以官銀盡買安寧等井私煎之鹽，並發州縣銷售，欲以彌縫虧空。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year of Qianlong Salt Controller Jiang Jixun used government silver to buy all privately boiled salt from Anning and other wells and issued it to prefectures and counties for sale, wishing to cover deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year of Qianlong Salt Controller Jiang Jixun used government silver to buy all privately boiled salt from Anning and other wells and pushed it on the counties for sale, hoping to paper over deficits.

sentences.zh: 額鹽積壓愈多，於是州縣又有計口授鹽、短秤加課之弊。

translations.literal: Quota salt piled up ever more; then prefectures and counties again had the abuses of allotting salt by head count and short-weight scales with added levies.
translations.idiomatic: Quota salt piled up ever higher; counties then revived abuses such as allotting salt by head count and short weights with extra levies.

sentences.zh: 煙戶無論男女老幼，皆應交課，窮困已極。

translations.literal: Smoking households, whether male or female, old or young, all had to pay the levy; destitution reached its limit.
translations.idiomatic: Every smoking household, man or woman, old or young, had to pay the levy; poverty reached its limit.

sentences.zh: 迤西一帶，遂至聚眾抗官，斃差焚屋。

translations.literal: In the western reaches crowds rose to resist officials, killed runners, and burned houses.
translations.idiomatic: In the western districts people gathered to resist officials, killed couriers, and burned houses.

sentences.zh: 前年威遠倮夷滋擾，即有此等奸民。

translations.literal: The year before, when the Yi of Weiyuan made trouble, there were such wicked men among them.
translations.idiomatic: The year before, when the Yi of Weiyuan stirred up trouble, such wicked men were among them.

sentences.zh: 祿豐一案，亦由鹽務起釁，江蘭並匿情不奏。

translations.literal: The Lufeng case also arose from salt affairs; Jiang Lan moreover concealed the facts and did not memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: The Lufeng affair likewise sprang from the salt monopoly; Governor Jiang Lan also concealed the facts and never reported them.

sentences.zh: 富綱到滇，實見有不得不改章以甦民困者。

translations.literal: When Fu Gang reached Yunnan he truly saw that regulations had to be changed to relieve the people’s distress.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Gang reached Yunnan he truly saw that the rules had to change to relieve the people’s distress.

sentences.zh: 竊思滇鹽官運官銷，積弊難返，應如督臣所奏，改為就井收課，聽民自便。」

translations.literal: He reflected that Yunnan salt under government transport and government sale had accumulated abuses hard to reverse, and it should be as the governor-general memorialized: changed to collecting tax at the well and letting the people do as they pleased.”
translations.idiomatic: He judged that government transport and government sale had entrenched abuses beyond repair and that, as the governor-general proposed, tax should be collected at the well and the people left free to trade.”

sentences.zh: 於是損益原奏，令灶戶自煎自賣，商販領照，聽其所之，試行二三年，再定各井歲額，下部議行。

translations.literal: He then adjusted the original proposal: furnace households were to boil and sell for themselves, merchants were to take licenses and go where they would; a trial of two or three years was set, after which annual quotas per well would be fixed and sent to the ministry for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He then revised the original plan: furnace households would boil and sell on their own, merchants would take licenses and go where they wished; after a trial of two or three years annual quotas per well would be set and sent to the ministry for approval.

sentences.zh: 又籌置堡田，免徭役加派，滇民感之。

translations.literal: He also planned garrison fields and exempted corvée and extra levies; the people of Yunnan were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He also set aside garrison fields and exempted corvée and extra levies; the people of Yunnan were grateful.

sentences.zh: 劾前撫江蘭匿抱母、恩耕二井水災不奏，蘭因黜罷。

translations.literal: He impeached the former governor Jiang Lan for concealing floods at the Baomu and Engeng wells and not reporting; Lan was therefore dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached former Governor Jiang Lan for concealing floods at the Baomu and Engeng wells; Lan was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 六年，自陳親老，乞改京職，允之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he stated that his parents were aged and begged transfer to a capital post; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he pleaded that his parents were aged and asked for a capital post; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 以貴州巡撫伊桑阿代。

translations.literal: Governor of Guizhou Yisang’a replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Yisang’a, governor of Guizhou, replaced him.

sentences.zh: 途次劾伊桑阿驕奢乖戾，苛派屬員，剿石峴苗飾詞冒功。

translations.literal: On the road he impeached Yisang’a for arrogance, luxury, perversity, harsh exactions from subordinates, and dressing up the campaign against the Shixian Miao as merit.
translations.idiomatic: En route he impeached Yisang’a for arrogance, luxury, perversity, harsh exactions from subordinates, and inflating the campaign against the Shixian Miao into false merit.

sentences.zh: 遣使勘實，置伊桑阿於法。

translations.literal: He sent agents to verify the facts and punished Yisang’a according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He sent agents to verify the facts and punished Yisang’a by law.

sentences.zh: 回京，授刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was appointed vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he was appointed vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 七年，偕副都統富尼善往貴州按事，劾巡撫常明鉛廠之弊，褫職治罪，即代署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, together with Vice Commander-in-Chief Funishan, he went to Guizhou to investigate affairs, impeached Governor Chang Ming for abuses in the lead mines, stripped and punished him, and at once acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he went to Guizhou with Vice Commander-in-Chief Funishan to investigate, impeached Governor Chang Ming for abuses in the lead mines, stripped and punished him, and immediately acted as governor.

sentences.zh: 尋調署雲南巡撫，劾布政使陳孝升、迤西道薩榮安以維西軍務冒帑，治如律。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to act as governor of Yunnan, impeached Provincial Administration Commissioner Chen Xiaosheng and Western Circuit Intendant Sa Rong’an for embezzling military funds in Weixi, and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to act as governor of Yunnan, impeached Administration Commissioner Chen Xiaosheng and Western Circuit Intendant Sa Rong’an for embezzling Weixi military funds, and punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕侍郎額勒布清查陝西軍需，自巡撫秦承恩以下，黜罰有差。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Vice Minister Elebu, he audited Shaanxi military supplies; from Governor Qin Chengen downward, dismissals and penalties varied.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, with Vice Minister Elebu, he audited Shaanxi military supplies; from Governor Qin Chengen down, dismissals and penalties varied.

sentences.zh: 調工部侍郎，又調戶部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of works and again to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of works and then to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 九年，誤聽湖北巡撫高杞言，劾湖廣總督吳熊光受賄，不得實，後復以獨對時密諭私告杞，事覺，下廷臣議罪，以大辟上。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he mistakenly believed Hubei Governor Gao Qi, impeached Huguang Governor-General Wu Xiongguang for taking bribes without establishing the facts, and later was found to have privately told Qi a secret instruction given in private audience; when this came to light the court deliberated punishment and recommended death.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he wrongly believed Hubei Governor Gao Qi, impeached Huguang Governor-General Wu Xiongguang for bribery without proof, and was later found to have privately relayed to Qi a secret instruction from a private audience; exposed, the court deliberated punishment and recommended death.

sentences.zh: 仁宗知彭齡無他，不欲因言事加重譴，詔斥諸臣所擬過當，有意杜言事者之口；

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor knew Pengling had no other fault and did not wish to increase punishment because of memorializing; he issued an edict that the court’s recommendation was excessive and aimed to stop the mouths of those who spoke on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Renzong Emperor knew Pengling had no other fault and did not wish to punish memorializing itself; he issued an edict that the court’s sentence was excessive and aimed to silence critics.

sentences.zh: 又念彭齡親老，免遠謫，罷職家居。

translations.literal: Again mindful that Pengling’s parents were aged, he spared distant banishment and dismissed him to live at home.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful too that Pengling’s parents were aged, he spared distant exile and dismissed him to live at home.

sentences.zh: 逾年，起授右庶子，驟遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was raised to right assistant reader of the heir apparent and soon vaulted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was restored as right assistant reader of the heir apparent and soon vaulted to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，偕侍郎英和往陝西讞獄，途經山西，命察議河東鹽務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, together with Vice Minister Ying He, he went to Shaanxi to judge cases; passing through Shanxi he was ordered to investigate and deliberate on Hedong salt affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, with Vice Minister Ying He, he went to Shaanxi to judge cases; passing Shanxi he was ordered to investigate Hedong salt affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋授安徽巡撫。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed governor of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed governor of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 壽州武舉張大有因妒姦毒斃族侄張倫及僱工人，總督鐵保徇蘇州知府週鍔以自中蛇毒定讞，彭齡推鞫得實，詔嘉之，特予議敘，鐵保等降黜有差。

translations.literal: At Shouzhou the military licentiate Zhang Dayou, out of jealous adultery, poisoned his clansman Zhang Lun and a hired worker to death. Governor-General Tie Bao followed Suzhou Prefect Zhou E in ruling death by self-inflicted snake venom. Pengling re-examined the case and established the truth; the emperor praised this, specially granted him a merit citation, and Tie Bao and others were demoted to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouzhou the military licentiate Zhang Dayou, jealous over an affair, poisoned his clansman Zhang Lun and a hired laborer. Governor-General Tie Bao followed Suzhou Prefect Zhou E in ruling death by self-inflicted snakebite. Pengling re-examined the case and proved murder; the emperor praised him, granted a special merit citation, and Tie Bao and others were demoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 十四年，奪情授貴州巡撫，固辭不起。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was appointed governor of Guizhou with mourning suspended, but firmly declined and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was appointed governor of Guizhou with mourning suspended, but firmly declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，署山西巡撫，遂實授。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he acted as governor of Shanxi and then received formal appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he served as acting governor of Shanxi and was soon confirmed in the post.

sentences.zh: 劾前巡撫成齡需索供應，又劾布政使劉清、署按察使張曾獻及府州縣多人，尋調陝西。

translations.literal: He impeached the former governor Cheng Ling for demanding supplies, again impeached Administration Commissioner Liu Qing, acting surveillance commissioner Zhang Cengxian, and many prefects and counties, and soon was transferred to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached former Governor Cheng Ling for extorting supplies, also impeached Administration Commissioner Liu Qing, acting Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Cengxian, and numerous prefectural and county officials, and was soon transferred to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 河東道劉大觀揭劾初彭齡任性乖張，命回山西聽勘，以怒斥前撫金應琦及瞻徇知府硃錫庚，部議革職，詔寬之，降補鴻臚寺卿。

translations.literal: Hedong Circuit Intendant Liu Daguan exposed a memorial impeaching Chu Pengling for willfulness and perversity; he was ordered back to Shanxi to await investigation. For angrily rebuking the former governor Jin Yingqi and showing favoritism toward Prefect Zhu Xigeng, the ministry deliberated dismissal from office; an edict was lenient and he was demoted to superintendent of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong Circuit Intendant Liu Daguan filed charges accusing Chu Pengling of willfulness and perversity; he was ordered back to Shanxi to await investigation. For angrily denouncing former Governor Jin Yingqi and favoring Prefect Zhu Xigeng, the ministry recommended dismissal; the emperor was lenient and demoted him to superintendent of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: He was transferred to intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed intendant of Shuntian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十六年，偕尚書托津清查南河工帑，劾罷廳營四十八員，复偕尚書崇祿往福建讞獄。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, together with Minister Tuojin, he audited the southern canal works treasury and impeached and removed forty-eight bureau officers; again together with Minister Chonglu he went to Fujian to judge cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he joined Minister Tuojin in auditing the southern canal works treasury and impeached forty-eight bureau officers; later he went with Minister Chonglu to Fujian to judge cases.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎，署浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of works and acted as governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of works and appointed acting governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 尋命往兩湖按訊湖北按察使周季堂及湖南學政徐松，季堂無貪跡，惟袒庇屬員，褫職，免治罪；

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to the two Hu to investigate Hubei Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Jitang and Hunan Education Commissioner Xu Song. Jitang had no trace of greed but shielded subordinates; he was stripped of office but spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to the two Hu to investigate Hubei Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Jitang and Hunan Education Commissioner Xu Song. Jitang showed no greed but sheltered his subordinates; he was stripped of office but not punished.

sentences.zh: 松需索陋規，出題割裂聖經，褫職遣戍。

translations.literal: Song demanded customary fees, set examination topics that mutilated the classics, was stripped of office and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Song extorted customary fees and set examination topics that mangled the classics; he was stripped of office and exiled.

sentences.zh: 十七年，調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 時兩江總督百齡劾南河總督陳鳳翔誤啟智、禮兩壩，鳳翔已被譴，自訴辯，又訐百齡信任鹽巡道硃爾賡額督辦葦蕩失當，命彭齡、松筠往按。

translations.literal: At that time Liangjiang Governor-General Bai Ling impeached Southern Canal Governor-General Chen Fengxiang for mistakenly opening the Zhi and Li barrages. Fengxiang had already been punished, pleaded in his own defense, and again accused Bai Ling of trusting Salt Patrol Commissioner Zhu Ergeng’e to supervise reed marshes improperly; Pengling and Songyun were ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang Governor-General Bai Ling then impeached Southern Canal Governor-General Chen Fengxiang for wrongly opening the Zhi and Li barrages. Fengxiang had already been censured, argued in his defense, and accused Bai Ling of trusting Salt Patrol Commissioner Zhu Ergeng’e to oversee reed marshes improperly; Pengling and Songyun were ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 百齡於啟壩時實同畫諾，遂請薄懲百齡，而硃爾賡額被重譴，語詳百齡等傳。

translations.literal: Bai Ling had in fact jointly approved when the barrages were opened; he therefore requested light punishment for Bai Ling, while Zhu Ergeng’e received heavy censure—the details are in the biographies of Bai Ling and others.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ling had in fact co-signed the order to open the barrages; Pengling therefore asked for leniency toward Bai Ling while Zhu Ergeng’e received heavy punishment, as set forth in the biographies of Bai Ling and others.

sentences.zh: 署南河總督，尋調倉場侍郎。

translations.literal: He acted as Southern Canal governor-general and soon was transferred to grain transport vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting Southern Canal governor-general and was soon transferred to grain transport vice minister.

sentences.zh: 十九年，命往廣西按訊巡撫成林，以恣意聲色，用度侈靡，褫成林職，籍其家。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was ordered to Guangxi to investigate Governor Cheng Lin; for indulging in music and women and extravagant expenditure, Cheng Lin was stripped of office and his property confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was sent to Guangxi to investigate Governor Cheng Lin; for indulging in pleasure and lavish spending, Cheng Lin was dismissed and his estate confiscated.

sentences.zh: 擢兵部尚書，特命署江蘇巡撫，清查虧空，疏言：「虧空應立時懲辦，而各省督撫往往密奏，僅使分限完繳。

translations.literal: He was promoted to minister of war and specially ordered to act as governor of Jiangsu to audit deficits. In his memorial he stated: “Deficits ought to be punished at once, yet governors-general and governors of the provinces often memorialize in secret and only require payment by installments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of war and specially ordered to act as governor of Jiangsu to audit fiscal shortfalls. His memorial read: “Shortfalls should be punished immediately, yet provincial governors often file secret memorials and merely require installment repayment.

sentences.zh: 始則屬官玩法，任意侵欺；

translations.literal: At first subordinate officials treated the law lightly and embezzled at will.
translations.idiomatic: At first subordinates treated the law lightly and embezzled at will.

sentences.zh: 繼則上司市恩，設法掩蓋。

translations.literal: Then superiors traded favors and devised means to cover it up.
translations.idiomatic: Then superiors traded favors and devised ways to cover the losses.

sentences.zh: 是以清查為續虧出路，密奏為緩辦良圖，請飭禁。」

translations.literal: Thus audits became a path to continued deficits and secret memorials a good scheme for delay; he requested strict prohibition.”
translations.idiomatic: Thus audits became a path to fresh deficits and secret memorials a scheme to stall punishment; he asked that both be forbidden.”

sentences.zh: 帝韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 劾江寧布政使陳桂生、江蘇布政使常格催徵不力，並褫職。

translations.literal: He impeached Jiangning Administration Commissioner Chen Guisheng and Jiangsu Administration Commissioner Chang Ge for slack collection and stripped both of office.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Jiangning Administration Commissioner Chen Guisheng and Jiangsu Administration Commissioner Chang Ge for slack tax collection and stripped both of office.

sentences.zh: 尋巡撫張師誠回任，仍命彭齡會同清查。

translations.literal: Soon Governor Zhang Shicheng returned to his post, but Pengling was still ordered to join in the audit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Governor Zhang Shicheng resumed his post, yet Pengling was still ordered to assist in the audit.

sentences.zh: 彭齡與百齡、師誠意不合，各擬章程，上詔斥其不能和衷。

translations.literal: Pengling was at odds in intent with Bai Ling and Shicheng; each drafted regulations, and the emperor issued an edict rebuke for their failure to work in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Pengling clashed with Bai Ling and Shicheng; each drafted his own regulations, and the emperor rebuked them for failing to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 既而疏劾百齡、師誠受關道鹽員饋銀，又劾陳桂生弊混，命大學士托津、尚書景安往按，至則百齡、師誠嗾屬員多方沮格，所劾並不得實。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized impeaching Bai Ling and Shicheng for accepting silver from customs and salt officials, and again impeached Chen Guisheng for mixed abuses. Grand Secretary Tuojin and Minister Jing An were ordered to investigate; on arrival Bai Ling and Shicheng incited subordinates to obstruct in many ways, and none of the charges was established.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that Bai Ling and Shicheng had accepted silver from customs and salt officials and again accused Chen Guisheng of mixed abuses. Grand Secretary Tuojin and Minister Jing An were sent to investigate; on arrival Bai Ling and Shicheng had their subordinates obstruct the inquiry at every turn, and none of the charges held.

sentences.zh: 上以彭齡性褊急，嫉惡過嚴，斥其輕躁，降內閣學士，召回京。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Pengling’s nature was narrow and urgent and his hatred of evil too severe, rebuked his rashness, demoted him to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and recalled him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Judging Pengling narrow and harsh in his hatred of evil, the emperor rebuked his rashness, demoted him to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat, and recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 茅豫者，以部員隨赴廣西，因留江蘇佐理，改知府。

translations.literal: Mao Yu had followed as a ministry clerk on the mission to Guangxi, remained in Jiangsu to assist, and was made prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Yu had accompanied him to Guangxi as a ministry clerk, stayed in Jiangsu to assist, and was made prefect.

sentences.zh: 至是彭齡疏陳豫兩耳重聽，代為乞假。

translations.literal: At this time Pengling memorialized that Yu was deaf in both ears and begged leave on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Pengling now memorialized that Mao Yu was deaf in both ears and begged leave on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 詔斥越職專擅，再降，以翰林院侍讀、侍講候補。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked overstepping authority and acting on one’s own; he was demoted again and made a candidate reader or expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him for overstepping authority; he was demoted again to candidate reader or expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 百齡复劾彭齡沉湎於酒，事一委茅豫，文致陳桂生之罪，私拆批摺，挾怨誣參；

translations.literal: Bai Ling again impeached Pengling for drowning himself in wine, leaving all affairs to Mao Yu, fabricating Chen Guisheng’s crimes, privately opening memorials and reports, and impeaching out of spite.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Ling impeached Pengling again for drowning himself in wine, leaving all business to Mao Yu, fabricating Chen Guisheng’s crimes, opening memorials privately, and lodging charges out of spite.

sentences.zh: 且豫實非耳聾，亦徇欺。

translations.literal: Moreover Yu was in fact not deaf; this too was favoritism and deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Mao Yu was not in fact deaf; this too was favoritism and deceit.

sentences.zh: 上怒，褫彭齡職，停其母九旬恩賚，令閉門思過。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged, stripped Pengling of office, suspended the ninetieth-birthday favor for his mother, and ordered him to close his door and reflect on his faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raged, stripped Pengling of office, withheld the ninetieth-birthday favor for his mother, and ordered him to remain at home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，起為工部主事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was raised to director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was restored as director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，未歸，請改注籍順天，服闋，以員外郎用。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, had not yet returned home, and requested transfer of registration to Shuntian; when mourning ended he was used as a vice director.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother before returning home, requested registration in Shuntian, and after mourning served as a vice director.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，授禮部侍郎，尋擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed vice minister of rites and soon promoted to minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed vice minister of rites and soon promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 三年，萬壽節，與十五老臣宴，繪圖於萬壽山玉瀾堂，御製詩稱其耿介，優賚珍物。

translations.literal: In the third year, on the imperial birthday, he dined with the fifteen aged ministers; their portraits were painted at the Yulan Hall on Longevity Hill, and the emperor composed a poem praising his integrity and bestowed fine gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, at the imperial birthday feast for the fifteen aged ministers, his portrait was painted at the Yulan Hall on Longevity Hill; the emperor composed a poem praising his integrity and bestowed rare gifts.

sentences.zh: 四年，以年老休致，食半俸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on account of age he retired and received half salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he retired on account of age and received half salary.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，詔優恤。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; an edict granted generous condolence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died; the emperor ordered generous posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 論曰：甚矣直臣之不易為也！

translations.literal: The commentary says: How difficult it is to be a straight official!
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: How hard it is to be a truly upright official!

sentences.zh: 赤心為國，犯顏批鱗，而人主諒之。

translations.literal: With a loyal heart for the state, risking the ruler’s displeasure to remonstrate, and the sovereign understanding him.
translations.idiomatic: With a loyal heart for the state, speaking bluntly even at the risk of the ruler’s wrath, and the sovereign forgiving him—

sentences.zh: 苟有排異己市盛名之心，借徑梯榮，眾矢集焉；

translations.literal: If one has a mind to exclude others and trade on a reputation, using the path to climb to glory, the arrows of the multitude gather.
translations.idiomatic: if one harbors a mind to exclude rivals and trade on fame, using remonstrance as a ladder to glory, the arrows of the multitude gather.

sentences.zh: 況身罹負乘，或加之貪婪乎？

translations.literal: How much more if one personally falls into overloading the cart, or adds greed to it?
translations.idiomatic: How much worse if one overreaches his station, or adds greed to the bargain?

sentences.zh: 魁倫、廣興之所以不得其死也。

translations.literal: This is why Kui Lun and Guang Xing did not die a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Kui Lun and Guang Xing did not die natural deaths.

sentences.zh: 初彭齡雖亦褊躁，然實政清操，蹶而復起，克保令名，宜哉！

translations.literal: Chu Pengling, though also narrow and rash, truly had clean government and integrity; he stumbled yet rose again and kept a good name to the end—as he deserved!
translations.idiomatic: Chu Pengling, though narrow and rash as well, truly governed cleanly and held his integrity; he fell, rose again, and kept a good name to the end—as was only fitting!
